questions.question: Why is round-robin load balancing actively harmful for cached LLM inference?
options: Round-robin cannot handle GPU nodes with different memory capacities
It routes requests to replicas that do not hold the request's prefix, forcing a full prefill instead of a cache hit
Round-robin creates hot spots by concentrating traffic on the first replica alphabetically
It does not support multi-region deployments across availability zones
questions.explanation: Cache-aware routing depends on landing each request on the replica holding its prefix KV blocks. Round-robin ignores this, so most requests miss the cache and pay full prefill cost (~800 ms) instead of the cache-hit cost (~80 ms) — a 10x TTFT penalty.

questions.question: What is the approximate TTFT difference between a cache hit and a cache miss on a long prompt in production?
options: ~10 ms hit vs ~20 ms miss (2x)
~80 ms hit vs ~800 ms miss (10x)
~200 ms hit vs ~400 ms miss (2x)
~500 ms hit vs ~5,000 ms miss (10x)
questions.explanation: The lesson cites: cache hit ~80 ms, cache miss (full cold prefill) ~800 ms — approximately 10x gap. This is the production penalty for routing that ignores KV cache locality.

questions.question: What percentage of LLM disaster-recovery failures are caused by teams backing up model weights but forgetting tokenizer files or quantization configs?
questions.explanation: The lesson cites 32% of LLM DR failures occur because teams backed up weights but forgot tokenizer files or quantization configs. The three-file DR checklist includes tokenizer.json/tokenizer.model, quantization configs, and engine config files.

questions.question: What approach do commercial cross-region inference offerings like Bedrock cross-region inference and GKE multi-cluster gateways optimize for?
options: KV cache locality and TTFT optimization across regions
Availability and failover, not TTFT or cache hit rate
Cost optimization by routing to the cheapest available region
Compliance by ensuring requests stay within data-residency boundaries
questions.explanation: The lesson distinguishes commercial offerings from KV-aware routing: Bedrock CRI and GKE multi-cluster gateways treat inference as opaque. They handle availability and failover but have no knowledge of KV cache state — they cannot improve TTFT via locality.

questions.question: How long did it take JPMorgan and Mayo Clinic to complete a us-east-1 failover in November 2024?
options: ~5 minutes
~22 minutes
~2 hours
~8 hours
questions.explanation: JPMorgan and Mayo Clinic ran a us-east-1 failover in November 2024 at approximately 22 minutes — meeting their 30-minute SLA. This is cited as a real-world DR reference point.

questions.question: A cache-aware router uses prefix-hash matching to route requests. What is the tie-breaker when two replicas hold the same prefix?
options: Alphabetical order by replica ID
GPU utilization — route to the less loaded replica
Request queue depth — route to the shorter queue
Network latency — route to the nearest replica
questions.explanation: The lesson describes the cache-aware router algorithm: primary routing is prefix-hash match; when two replicas both hold the prefix, the tie-breaker is GPU utilization — route to the less loaded replica to avoid creating a hot spot.
